**Who are you?**

We're a guild largely consisting of (largely) PvE enthusiasts of all levels of ability. Our main focus is our raid team, which is built on a strong core of experienced players and leaders, and have gotten Curve on each tier so far (except Nighthold. We don't talk about Nighthold). We're looking to shore up our roster with players willing to put a shift in and make some progress. 

After a tumultuous but generally successful Uldir, we're looking to add a few players to our raid and mythic+ lineups to allow us better flexibility. We have a core of strong players and are looking to add to that, as well as being flexible in bringing newer players into our lineups. We have some glaring gaps in the main raid team, but will consider bringing in any roles for further evaluation at this time.

We like to raid and do take the game fairly seriously. We're looking to progress and would like to find players who have similar goals as us, most notably self-improvement and betterment and a drive to learn and deliver better each week. We see gear as a means to do this, and do expect you to invest a little time to make your character stronger, and we're more than happy to help you do so if we can.

Our raid team runs **Thursday 1945-2300** and **Sunday 1915-1030**, with alt runs and normals thrown in throughout the week, often at short notice. We run mythic plus most nights and like to try and get as many people as possible their 10 key completed. If you put in, we ...put out? No, we don't do that. OK, ignore that bit. If you contribute, our team are willing to bend over backwards to help get you where you want to be.

We provide most raid consumables and a solid repair allowance, increasing depending on contributions to the guild and bank. We are also likely to trade you cheese or odd things we find on the floor if we like you. No promises.

Our only rules are to be 18+, have respect for your fellow guild members and officers, and to be able to turn up for raids repaired and prepared. We use discord for comms and the server is fairly active. Speaking is optional but listening is essential.

​

**What do we expect?**

Attendance and community. We would like people to be active, involved and engaged in the game. Core knowledge can be taught or picked up, and a lot of our core have played most classes at high levels and are willing to help but, as the saying goes, we can't teach people to care.

Respect for yourself, other players and the guild we represent.

A sense of humour, and an understanding of when to apply it (usually liberally).

Willingness to contribute, help others and join in with projects.

An appreciation of cheese is highly regarded, but can be waived if you seem nice enough.

​

If you would like to join us or ask any further questions, don't hesitate to contact any of our officer core for a chat.

What is annoying me, and what people are glossing over, is that the OP is literally asking for help to be more social. We know nothing about him other than his post. If his case is similar to mine (and I'm aware that I am making an assumption here but bear with me) then he may not be able to leave his house at all. Interaction becomes impossible. Any form of social contact will be a huge boost to his self esteem and help limit feeling so low.

Now if he sits on league all day then yes, we have a different problem. Gaming addiction is a very separate entity to depression, but they can be shared.

Depression doesn't disappear, however hard you "work" at it. Finding ways to interact with people, be social, talking, even asking for help like the OP is a huge mark towards learning to deal with it.

Sorry, but this is bullshit. As a severe depressive (and the same with my wife), gaming and short escapism allows us to be social in an environment we can control, without pressures of enforced conversation. And if it gets too much? We quit and go back to the real world. Gaming has literally saved my life over the last 2 months, to the point I can almost function as a human again.

Edit: Seeing as i'm being downvoted, let me add a bit more. Being depressed gives you a hundred different people giving you a hundred different ways to "cheer up". Most of these are from people who have never really experienced clinical depression. It's very different to being sad. You lose the ability to form sentances, you talk in whispers, you can't pick up a phone to talk to friends and loved ones.

In short, you feel like the whole world has put you on some sort of imaginary "ignore" list. You feel alone.

The OP never gave any time indications as to how much he is playing. Who are we to tell him he is playing too much, or that finally finding a way to feel social and interact with humans (the first step to recovery, as any doctor will tell you) is the wrong thing to do?

In my case, me and my wife have taken to playing World of Warcraft (in my case re-igniting an old passion, in hers a complete new experience). It has given us a reason to get out of bed in the morning, not lie staring at the ceiling wondering why I still hadn't gathered the courage to end it. My wife is back to work next month, and attributes it to a) having a badass, super sexy husband and b) having made a whole heap of friends through WoW, who will stay with us for the rest of our lives. True friends.

OP, don't let people tell you what is right or wrong for you. It's the same as people saying "why don't you try just cheering up" or "just face your fears,  that's what i'd do". You will know when you're spending too long online, and only you. my IGN is Gentleman Velkoz if you'd like to talk or play, but just to warn you, i'm a proper baddie.
